scene_rule: Scenes are chosen by a rule that reads no position error: among all stretches of one window in which every row of the build has a synced sensor moment and follows the row before it by one stride, the 4 longest are taken, the earlier window first on a tie, and each scene is the first 12 s of its stretch.
notes: Each scene is a stretch of one window of the held-out game. The private site plays the clip, the public site shows the still.

frames holds the build's rows, about ten a second. t is the time of a row in seconds from the first frame of the clip; the boxes of a row belong to the clip frame at that time. fps, width and height describe the clip.

A box is matched when it was assigned to a sensor player within 5 ft, the matching distance of the scorecard; otherwise it is unmatched (the scorecard calls such a box a ghost box). broadcast holds the court position of every matched box and of every unmatched box that lands within 10 ft of the court; truth holds the ten sensor players of the synced moment.

error_ft, p50_error_ft and p90_error_ft are distances between matched pairs through the build's own homography. Pairs farther apart than the matching distance are not matched, so these values are biased low and are not the scorecard's measurement.

Show a scene's error beside the whole-game value of the scorecard for build r23: p50 1.92 ft and p90 4.98 ft over 11292 matched players on 1447 testable rows (reports/scorecard/gsw_phx_2016__r23.json).
4 unmatched boxes land farther than 10 ft from the court and have no court position in broadcast.

The build read some stretches a few frames late. The clip of a scene starts at the frame the build really read for the scene's first row, so t needs no correction. The still is the frame of the scene's middle row, at still_t.
truth is empty in this copy: the sensor positions of the synced moments are on the private copy only (PLAN.md D60). boxes, broadcast and error_ft are kept.
